Create something like `append_dummy_log.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_FILE="${1:-/var/log/openclaw-dummy.log}"
SLEEP_MIN="${SLEEP_MIN:-0.2}"
SLEEP_MAX="${SLEEP_MAX:-1.5}"

rand_str() {
  # 24 chars URL-safe-ish
  tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 24
}

while true; do
  ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  line="$ts $(rand_str)"

  if [[ -w "$LOG_FILE" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >>"$LOG_FILE"
  else
    # fall back to sudo if needed
    printf '%s\n' "$line" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE" >/dev/null
  fi

  # random sleep between min/max using awk (portable)
  awk -v min="$SLEEP_MIN" -v max="$SLEEP_MAX" 'BEGIN{srand(); print min+rand()*(max-min)}' | xargs sleep
done
```

Update the loop to check available space on the filesystem that holds the log, and exit only when it hits 0 bytes available:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

LOG_FILE="${1:-/var/log/openclaw-dummy.log}"
SLEEP_MIN="${SLEEP_MIN:-0.2}"
SLEEP_MAX="${SLEEP_MAX:-1.5}"

rand_str() { tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 24; }

avail_bytes() {
  # Available bytes on the filesystem containing LOG_FILE
  df -PB1 -- "$(dirname -- "$LOG_FILE")" | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}'
}

while true; do
  avail="$(avail_bytes || echo 0)"
  if [[ "${avail:-0}" -le 0 ]]; then
    exit 0
  fi

  ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  line="$ts $(rand_str)"

  if [[ -w "$LOG_FILE" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >>"$LOG_FILE"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$line" | sudo tee -a "$LOG_FILE" >/dev/null
  fi

  awk -v min="$SLEEP_MIN" -v max="$SLEEP_MAX" 'BEGIN{srand(); print min+rand()*(max-min)}' | xargs sleep
done
```

Note: this will intentionally fill the disk until the filesystem reports 0 available bytes (which can destabilize a system). If you want a safer variant (stop at a threshold like 1–5% free), tell me the cutoff.
